title: Modular FastAPI application composition with APIRouter

steps.title: The rule: Modular FastAPI application composition with APIRouter

blocks.text: Create an APIRouter for a feature's operations and register those operations on that router rather than requiring all handlers to live in the main module.

Import feature routers and call app.include_router(router) to assemble their operations into the application. An include_router prefix adds to the included operations' paths, and tags, dependencies and responses can be supplied at inclusion.

blocks.code:
# orders.py
from fastapi import APIRouter
router = APIRouter()
@router.get('/orders')
def list_orders():
    return []

# main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()
from orders import router
app.include_router(router, prefix='/api')

annotations.text: Register feature operations on an APIRouter, then import and include it in the application assembly module. Defining the router alone does not assemble it. Including a local /orders operation with prefix /api produces /api/orders. The include point can also supply tags, dependencies, and responses.

segments.label: Register feature operations on APIRouter and include them in the application
segments.summary: APIRouter organizes related operations in separate modules. Create a router in a feature module, then register operations with router.get or router.post instead of app.get or app.post. The main module includes the router with app.include_router. Moving existing operations into feature modules can preserve their external URLs and behavior while improving internal organization. Inclusion also supports common prefixes and tags.

# Supplied feature-module boundary; the sandbox assembles it in one entry file.

orders_result = "synthetic-orders"
router = APIRouter()
def list_orders(): return orders_result

# Supplied single-file feature-module loader, used only because the runner executes one entry.
import sys, types
feature_module = types.ModuleType("orders")
feature_module.router = router
sys.modules["orders"] = feature_module

solution_files.content:
from fastapi import FastAPI, APIRouter
# Supplied feature-module boundary; the sandbox assembles it in one entry file.
app = FastAPI()
orders_result = "synthetic-orders"
router = APIRouter()
@router.get("/orders")
def list_orders(): return orders_result

# Supplied single-file feature-module loader, used only because the runner executes one entry.
import sys, types
feature_module = types.ModuleType("orders")
feature_module.router = router
sys.modules["orders"] = feature_module
from orders import router
app.include_router(router, prefix="/api")

def router_paths(scope):
    routes = router.routes if scope == "feature" else app.routes
    return [r.path for r in routes if "orders" in r.path]
